_comment: Written by the trading runs (9:30a / hourly / 3:30p ET). Never contains account numbers, broker IDs, or any account other than the sandbox.

account.note: Cash account. Proceeds settle T+1. Re-read live at 12:22 ET from the broker and unchanged for the fourth read running: 128.90 total, all of it cash, nothing unsettled, so deployable is the full balance. No equity or option positions are open, which is why the third mid-session run also had no exit to enforce.

entryWatch.trigger: Reaction strong and still holding 30-60 min after the 8/5 open
entryWatch.why: Still dead, but for the first time today the read moved toward it rather than away. AMD is bid 488.79 at 12:22 ET against a 518.58 official close, about -5.7%, off the 482.06 low read an hour ago and back above the 486.55 at 10:22. Three hours of writing 'the gap is extending' and then an hour where it is not is worth saying plainly. It does not open the setup: a continuation needs a strong reaction to continue, and a bounce off the low of a 5.7% gap down is a less-bad reaction, not a strong one. A thesis killed by direction is not revived by a partial retrace of the move that killed it.

entryWatch.trigger: Reaction strong but the leader is already extended
entryWatch.why: Conditional on a strong leader, and the leader is still down 5.7% on the day even after bouncing. There is no upside chain to find a laggard in. SMCI, the name this read pointed at, is bid 31.17 and down about 1.6% - better than the -2.4% an hour ago, and still following the leader's move rather than lagging one.

entryWatch.trigger: A pullback that holds on 8/6 or 8/7, not today's reaction bar
entryWatch.why: Still the one live catalyst on the list, and still the one entry the rulebook explicitly forbids today. UPST reported 8/4 after the bell and is bid 31.63 at 12:22 ET against a 30.32 close, about +4.3%. That is the reaction day itself, which checklist item 2 calls a wait signal. The full intraday sequence is now 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 open, 32.36, 32.05, 31.63 - a reaction day that has bled all session and sits 0.60 below its own open bid. That is an argument for the day-2/3 pullback setup and against buying anything today. A spike leaking is not a pullback; a pullback is a session that opens after the reaction day and holds.

entryWatch.trigger: Leader gapped down, most of the list red, only catalyst is a reaction-day spike
entryWatch.why: The branch the open resolved to and the position the account is still in three hours later. Eight of the nine candidates are red at 12:22 with OKLO's +0.3% the only green print, and four of the nine report tonight. The third hour is the first to move a price in a helpful direction - AMD's bounce - and it still changed no flag, because the level that would change one was never close. A one-position account has no way to be wrong cheaply here, and deployable cash keeps for a setup that fits.

candidatesAsOf: 2026-08-05 12:22 ET, live session bids. The Last column is the official 8/4 settled close.
candidatesNote: Bids are live and quoted as bids, never marks. Re-read at 12:22 ET by the third mid-session run. Earnings 8/11 after the close, which lands inside a five-session time stop opened today, so any entry needs the straddle pulled under item 3 rather than being treated as an earnings-free name. Bid 31.17, about -1.6%; the sympathy read needs a leader that is up, and the leader is down 5.7%.
